paragraphs: Liverpool City Council runs its own fostering service, and the independent agencies shown above also approve carers in the city. The council says it is responsible for more than 1,500 looked-after children. Fostering for the council means caring for Liverpool children close to their friends, schools and communities, with the council's social workers behind you; an independent agency assesses, approves and supervises you itself and offers homes to children placed by councils.

Liverpool recruits through Foster4, a hub shared with neighbouring councils and backed by the Department for Education. When it launched in May 2024 the eight councils had more than 4,600 children in care between them and just over 1,150 approved council foster carers. By October 2025, when the Foster4 roadshow bus came to Church Street, the councils were citing more than 5,000 children in care and only 1,200 approved carers. Government funding announced in December 2023 put over £1 million into the recruitment hub and a further £1 million into extending Mockingbird.

Mockingbird groups nearby fostering families around an experienced hub carer, like an extended family. Liverpool's first group, launched in December 2024, brought ten foster families together, and the council announced its second hub in July 2026. Since March 2025 carers have also had the Liverpool Foster Care Association, run by foster carers for foster carers, with the council meeting it every quarter.

To foster with the council you need to be 21 or over and have a spare room. Council carers get Council Tax exemption, training before and after approval, free Lifestyles membership for the household, breaks at a council caravan at Presthaven, 24-hour emergency support, mentors, monthly forums and baby and toddler groups. Carers already with an agency can transfer, which the council aims to complete in eight to twelve weeks, and it says it can often match current fees. Family and friends who step in for a child are assessed and approved as foster carers too, starting with a visit from the child's social worker.

We do not yet publish a Liverpool pay page, so ask the council and two or three of the services above for their rates and compare their support. If you live near the city's edge, the Knowsley, Sefton and Wirral pages list more services.
